verdicts.title: The only epsilon-value regression test for the CachedProcess repeated_pld bug (OPQ-005) was deleted; the surviving guards use the one strategy where the buggy and correct answers are bit-identical
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual link reproduced. `git show 819ef0d9 -- packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py` shows `class TestCachedPerStepRepeatedPld` (with `e_wrong = step.pld().self_compose(K).epsilon_at(_DELTA)` and `assert e_wrong > e_horizon * 1.5`, and a docstring naming the Identity degeneracy) deleted in the same commit that added `test_cached_horizon_step_preserves_prefix`. The surviving guard at packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py:172-178 uses `_proc()` = identity_strategy (lines 109-115) and asserts `(cached_step * 5).pld() is proc.pld_at(5)`. I re-ran the reporter's mutation (`del CachedProcess.repeated_pld`, packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/composition/_cached.py:86-108) over packages/opaque-accounting/tests + packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting and got exactly '2 failed, 579 passed, 1 skipped', both failures on `assert ... is ...` with identical-valued PLDs ('assert Pld(asymmetric, 105371 bins) is Pld(asymmetric, 105371 bins)'). I reproduced the degeneracy numerically: identity/n=10/K=5 gives 0.3165010449987564 for horizon, self_compose and cached alike; band_mf(bands=16)/n=128 gives horizon 0.35841322921357843 vs self_compose 0.7788310660598607 (2.173x) with cached matching the horizon. A grep over every test tree confirms no other test combines `acc.cached` with a correlated (band-MF/BLT) process, so no numeric assertion anywhere discriminates. Severity lowered from medium to low and affects_epsilon corrected to false: the relay is present and correct at 4b13d82, epsilon is right today, and the surviving `is` assertions do still fail closed under the mutation, so this is a hardening/coverage-quality item (restore a band-MF epsilon-value assertion), not a live defect. Not a duplicate of #683/#685 (those are code defects in horizon-prefix and cached-accountant continuation, not this regression-test gap).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No epsilon is wrong today. The residual risk is coverage shape: the only assertions that discriminate a missing `CachedProcess.repeated_pld` relay are two Python object-identity (`is`) checks, both on strategies (identity_strategy, RandomAllocation) where the correct horizon PLD and the buggy `pld().self_compose(K)` fallback are bit-identical in value (verified: 0.3165010449987564 for all three paths). Any future change that makes PLD object identity non-deterministic - a cache-eviction or memoization rework - invites relaxing `is` to `==`, at which point the suite retains zero coverage for the OPQ-005 failure mode, whose real cost is a 2.17x epsilon inflation on correlated strategies (band_mf bands=16, n_steps=128, sample_rate=0.01, delta=1e-5: 0.7788 reported vs 0.3584 correct).

verdicts.title: CI test-package matrix is a hand-maintained inventory with no coverage guard, after the auto-discovery script was deleted - and pyproject.toml still documents automatic pickup
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly. .github/workflows/python-tests.yml:62-89 hardcodes five `suite.paths` blocks naming ten package directories plus `tests`; `ls packages/` returns exactly those ten, so the inventory is complete today. .github/scripts/ contains no discover_package_matrices.py; `git log --diff-filter=D` confirms 938a8a56 (#676) deleted it and 5b2a2957 (#464) added it, and I read the deleted script - it did enumerate packages/*/pyproject.toml and emit `test_shards` plus build matrices, so the auto-discovery claim is accurate. No test or script anywhere asserts matrix completeness (grep over .github/scripts, tests/, packages/*/tests). pyproject.toml:163-170 still states 'any package with a `tests/` dir is picked up automatically. New packages, renames, and deletes don't need matching edits in CI ... Identical behavior locally and in CI' - false for CI as of #704. I also note .github/workflows/build-distributions.yml:73-74 hardcodes per-package build steps the same way, so a forgotten package would be neither tested nor built. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is a latent process risk with no current gap - the one package added during the delta (opaque-alignment) *was* added to the matrix (python-tests.yml:85) - and the fix is a ~10-line guard plus a comment correction. It does not duplicate #325 (packaging/supply-chain CI) since that issue predates the discovery-script deletion and covers a different surface.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A contributor adds packages/opaque-<new>/ with a tests/ tree and, trusting the pyproject.toml:164-170 comment that says CI picks packages up automatically, does not edit .github/workflows/python-tests.yml. Local `uv run pytest` runs the tests; every CI lane (PR, main, release gate) runs zero of them and the `Python tests` check stays green. The same happens on a package rename, which additionally makes the affected matrix leg collect nothing. Nothing currently detects either case; no package is actually missing from the matrix at 4b13d82.

verdicts.title: allow-empty-test-selection makes the distributed and CUDA lanes pass on zero collected tests, and two of five distributed suites already rely on that escape hatch
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:40-43 converts pytest exit 5 to exit 0 when ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION=true; the flag is set at pr.yml:80 (distributed) and pr.yml:144/159/176 (three CUDA lanes) and mirrored at ci.yml:45/104/116/130. I ran the distributed lane's exact marker one path at a time against the current tree: packages/opaque-base 0 collected (8 deselected), opaque-accounting 0 (97), opaque-auditing 0 (222), opaque-patches 0 (619), `tests` 0 (187); opaque-dpsgd collects 5/847. So the 'Foundation' and 'Integration' legs of the distributed lane execute nothing today and are converted to green. I also checked the only downstream consumer of the run record: .github/actions/upload-python-coverage/action.yml:20-27 treats an empty TEST_RESULTS_FILE as 'No package tests matched this group', skips coverage upload, and exits 0 - there is no floor anywhere on tests executed per lane. Severity stays low: the escape hatch is structurally necessary given heterogeneous marker/path grouping, and the specific regression it would mask (losing the `distributed`/`cuda` markers wholesale) is an unusual refactor. The fix is a per-lane minimum-collected assertion, not removing the flag.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A refactor removes or renames the `distributed` marker (e.g. `pytestmark = pytest.mark.distributed` dropped from packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py and its siblings while files move). All five distributed matrix legs then collect zero tests, each exits 5, each is converted to success by ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION, coverage upload is skipped with a notice, and 'Linux amd64 (distributed)' reports green having run no multi-rank test. Today two of the five legs (foundation, integration) already collect zero, verified, so the lane's green status carries no signal about how many of the remaining legs ran. The same shape applies to the three self-hosted CUDA lanes if the `cuda` marker is lost.

verdicts.title: The K-prefix invariant sweep was thinned to 4 sampled steps, dropping K=n-1 and every atomic-unit boundary, in the exact area covered by 8 open prefix-accounting issues
verdicts.reasoning: The diff is exactly as described (17cfae6a cut `checked_steps` from {1,M,n//2,n-1} u range(M,n+1,M) u {n} to {1,M,n//2,n} and reduced the monotonicity loop to {M,n//2,n}), but the two load-bearing consequences are false. (1) 'K=n-1 is no longer checked at all' - packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step_invariants.py:125-137, TestCyclicPoissonIdentity.test_monotonic_and_bounded_by_full, still evaluates points [1,5,25,50,100,150,199,200] at n=200 and asserts both monotonicity and bounded-by-full at k=199=n-1; #707 only merged and memoized that test, it did not thin it. (2) 'every atomic-unit boundary' dropped - TestCyclicPoissonBand.test_sandwich_at_every_step (line 186-207) still sweeps *every* K in range(1, 81) at n=80/M=8 asserting the atomic-unit sandwich, and test_monotonic_across_bands (line 209-212) still walks range(8,101,8) at n=100. The reporter's illustrative pair '(n=80, M=8), 10 monotonicity points down to 3' matches no entry in _SUPPORTED_PAIRS; I enumerated the real ones: CyclicPoisson/IdentityMf n=64 M=1, CyclicPoisson/BandMf n=64 M=4, BMinSep/BandMf n=32 M=4, and five BallsInBins pairs n=16 M=4. (3) Five of the eight parametrized pairs are Monte-Carlo paths, and since 88a25769 (#748) their prefixes fail closed to the full-horizon bound - test_prefix_invariants itself asserts `epsilons[M] == pytest.approx(e_full)` for MC procs - so a per-K monotonicity sweep over them is vacuous by construction. The only genuine residual is thinner deep-epoch coverage for BallsInBins/IdentityMf, whose dedicated test shrank from 10 bins x 10 epochs to 4 x 3; and #748 simultaneously *strengthened* the same test (exact bounds instead of 10%/15% MC slack, and test_sandwich_at_intermediate_K no longer skips MC paths). The claimed sensor blind spot at K=n-1 and at interior atomic boundaries does not exist.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No demonstrated blind spot. A prefix-PLD regression at K=n-1 would still be caught by TestCyclicPoissonIdentity.test_monotonic_and_bounded_by_full (k=199, n=200), and one at an interior atomic-unit boundary such as K=3M by TestCyclicPoissonBand.test_sandwich_at_every_step (every K in 1..80 at M=8) and test_monotonic_across_bands. The only measurable reduction is depth of BallsInBins-with-identity prefix coverage (horizon 100 -> 12 steps, monotonicity points 10 -> 3), which would let a regression confined to the 4th-or-later epoch of a balls-in-bins schedule pass; that is a narrow gap inside the scope of open issues #695/#698/#700.

verdicts.title: A test that creates a real Gloo process group and binds a port runs in the parallel lane, and fail-opens with a silent skip when it finds one already live
verdicts.reasoning: Every structural claim checks out: packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_trl_trainers.py:1914 carries only `@pytest.mark.slow`, unlike every other real-process-group test (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py, packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/ddp/test_dpftrl_cpu_gloo.py, packages/opaque-engine/tests/ddp/test_cpu_gloo.py all set `pytestmark = pytest.mark.distributed`); it therefore lands in the main-branch lane at ci.yml:30-40 (`not cuda and not mps and not distributed`, `-n auto --dist loadscope`) rather than the serial distributed lane (ci.yml:41-49, no xdist input). Lines 1942-1944 do bind-then-close to reserve a port that real_init consumes ~15 lines later, and lines 1934-1936 skip on `torch.distributed.is_initialized()`. What I could not establish is any trigger for either failure mode. The only other bind-then-close helper, tests/_support/opaque_test_support.py:80-85, is used exclusively by `distributed`-marked tests that never co-run in this lane; the ephemeral-port window is milliseconds against a ~28k-port range. And the `is_initialized()` self-skip has no contamination source: the only other in-process `init_process_group` call sites in the repo are packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py and test_ddp_trainer.py, both spawning subprocesses and both `distributed`-marked, and this test destroys its own group in a `finally`. I ran the test to completion: 1 passed in 2.81s. So this is a real marker/hygiene inconsistency (the test should carry `distributed` and should fail rather than skip on a live group) with no reproduced flake. Severity low, as reported.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Established: the only test that brings up a real Gloo process group outside the serial distributed lane runs under `-n auto --dist loadscope` on main, reserves a TCP port by bind-then-close and connects to it ~15 lines later, and turns any pre-existing live process group into a silent skip rather than a failure. Not established: any concrete trigger. No other in-process group initializer runs in that lane (the DDP-trainer tests spawn subprocesses and are `distributed`-marked), so the skip guard is currently inert, and the port race window is a few milliseconds against the ephemeral range. The residual exposure is that the DPO reference-forward ordering contract - the only test pinning it - would be silently unverified if a future test in the same xdist worker ever leaves a group initialized, and that worker assignment under `-n auto` is not stable across runners.

verdicts.title: New patched-vs-upstream parity suite silently pytest.skips gradient and vmap-grad parity for 4 of 26 registered model families, on the grounds that the patches change the backward Jacobian
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed and, for one family, stronger than reported. packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:85-93 defines `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {'gpt2','qwen3_next','deepseek_v4','gpt_oss'}` with the comment 'custom autograd functions in the patches that change the backward Jacobian path'; lines 269-270 and 456-457 turn that into bare `pytest.skip` inside test_backward_grads_parity and test_vmap_grad_parity; the coverage guard at 482-490 subtracts only `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {'qwen3_5_moe'}` and so is blind to those exemptions; `supported_families()` returns 26 entries including all four. `git log -S` confirms the set shipped with the suite in 5936552b (#481). I then cleared the skip set and re-ran. Result: test_vmap_grad_parity - the DP-relevant path, which builds a genuinely unpatched reference via build_patched_model_pair and compares per-example grads through `clipped_grad` (_test_utils.py:448-510) - PASSES for gpt_oss and deepseek_v4 (those two exemptions are stale), ERRORS for qwen3_next because the unpatched reference itself cannot run under vmap (transformers/masking_utils.py:1501 data-dependent control flow, an upstream limitation the skip cannot avoid), and genuinely FAILS for gpt2 with a large numerical mismatch, not roundoff: on `transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias` the patched per-example gradient reads 9.81e-3 where unpatched reads 6.20e-3. gpt2 forward-logits parity passes in the same run, matching the code comment that the forward is bit-identical while the backward is not. test_backward_grads_parity additionally fails for gpt_oss/deepseek_v4 on a structural key mismatch (`model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks` gradient missing on one side). affects_epsilon correctly false - clipping still bounds sensitivity. Overlaps open #330 ('Establish patched-versus-upstream numerical parity'), but I am keeping already_tracked 0: #330 asks for parity infrastructure to exist, and the new, actionable facts here are that the infrastructure now exists and is green while concealing a reproduced gradient mismatch in a family `supported_families()` advertises, and that two of the four exemptions no longer hold. Severity medium rather than low for the same reason: this is a confirmed numerical defect, not only missing verification.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user fine-tunes a GPT-2-family model with DPTrainer. `apply_model_patches` installs the kv_cache/batchify shims, and the per-example gradients that reach `clipped_grad` differ materially from the unpatched model's true per-example gradients - verified by clearing `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and running test_vmap_grad_parity[gpt2], which fails with 9.81e-3 vs 6.20e-3 on transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias while forward-logits parity passes. Clipping still bounds sensitivity so the privacy accounting stays valid, but training optimizes a different objective and the suite is green because gpt2 is skipped by name. Because the exemptions use `skip` rather than `xfail(strict=True)`, the suite also cannot report that gpt_oss and deepseek_v4 now pass vmap-grad parity (verified), so those two exemptions will persist indefinitely; qwen3_next is a genuine upstream vmap limitation in the reference, not a patch-fidelity finding.
